claude.sample_unit: domain-level RCT risk-of-bias assessments (300 per domain across 7 domains; 60 per domain in human-AI collaboration round)

links.outcome: Reviewer accuracy and intervention rate across human-AI collaboration modes for risk-of-bias assessment
links.effect: Accuracy under M2 and M3 ranged from 0.633 to 0.900; M2 achieved highest accuracy in most tasks; M3 markedly reduced intervention rates; LLM alone accuracy 0.403 to 0.777.
links.quote: Accuracy under M2 and M3 ranged from 0.633 to 0.900.

links.outcome: Human reviewer accuracy when shown model reasoning and disagreement cues versus evidence only
links.effect: M1 (evidence only) was never on the Pareto frontier; M2 (reasoning shown) had higher accuracy in five tasks, e.g., SB-IRSG 0.900 vs 0.817; M3 disagreement trigger cut intervention.
links.quote: M2 demonstrated higher accuracy in five tasks, while M3 showed a clear advantage in reducing intervention rates.

links.outcome: AI performance as used by human reviewers versus standalone model accuracy
links.effect: Standalone LLM accuracy ranged 0.403-0.777, while human-AI collaboration under M2/M3 reached 0.633-0.900 and improved consistency of human judgments.
links.quote: LLMs (like DeepSeek V3 and Qwen-plus) cannot yet replace human RoB assessment but well-designed Human-AI collaboration can improve accuracy and reduce manual workload.

links.outcome: Comparison of two candidate LLMs on risk-of-bias classification accuracy
links.effect: DeepSeek V3 outperformed Qwen-plus in four of seven domains (PB, AB, RB, OB); Qwen-plus slightly better in SB-IRSG, SB-IAC, DB.
links.quote: The results shown in Fig. 3 indicate that DeepSeek V3 outperforms Qwen-plus in the tasks of PB, AB, RB, and OB, whereas Qwen-plus performs slightly better in the tasks of SB-IRSG, SB-IAC, and DB.

links.outcome: Deferral to humans triggered by low confidence or model disagreement; accuracy and intervention rate
links.effect: Predictions with confidence >0.8 were 16.78% to 29.23% more accurate than those ≤0.8; M3 reduced intervention (e.g., DB -40%) with accuracy roughly maintained in structured tasks.
links.quote: Across the six domains (DB, SB-IRSG, PB, RB, OB, AB), model predictions with confidence scores above 0.8 consistently showed substantially higher accuracy than those with scores ≤ 0.8, with performance gaps ranging from 16.78% to 29.23% (Appendix 5).

links.outcome: Inter-rater agreement validating ground-truth reference labels
links.effect: Senior reviewer independently reassessed 60 RCTs per domain; Cohen's Kappa ranged from 0.724 to 0.942 across seven domains.
links.quote: The Cohen’s Kappa values ranged from 0.724 to 0.942 across all seven domains (Appendix 1), supporting its use as a high-fidelity reference standard for subsequent evaluation.

unlisted_practices: Two-model disagreement-triggered human review to reduce reviewer workload
Confidence-threshold-based routing (0.8) of LLM outputs to human review in evidence synthesis

links.effect: Senior reviewer reassessment Cohen’s Kappa values ranged from 0.724 to 0.942 across seven domains.
links.quote: The Cohen’s Kappa values ranged from 0.724 to 0.942 across all seven domains (Appendix 1), supporting its use as a high-fidelity reference standard for subsequent evaluation.

links.effect: DeepSeek V3 was higher in PB, AB, RB, OB; Qwen-plus was slightly higher in SB-IRSG, SB-IAC, DB.
links.quote: The results shown in Fig. 3 indicate that DeepSeek V3 outperforms Qwen-plus in the tasks of PB, AB, RB, and OB, whereas Qwen-plus performs slightly better in the tasks of SB-IRSG, SB-IAC, and DB.

links.effect: Standalone accuracy ranged 0.403 to 0.777; human-AI M2/M3 accuracy ranged 0.633 to 0.900.
links.quote: However, when integrated into a well-designed Human-AI collaboration framework, they can significantly improve both accuracy and efficiency, demonstrating strong application potential.

links.effect: M2 was highest in five tasks (Acc 0.675 to 0.900); M3 intervention was 0.083 to 0.467 across tasks.
links.quote: M2 demonstrated higher accuracy in five tasks, while M3 showed a clear advantage in reducing intervention rates.

links.effect: M3 versus M2: DB accuracy + 0.008 and intervention -0.400; AB intervention + 0.034 with no accuracy gain; RB accuracy + 0.042 and intervention + 0.333.
links.quote: In RB, although M3 significantly improves accuracy (+ 4.2%), it also leads to a substantial rise in human intervention (+ 33.3%), highlighting the current limitations of models in handling complex outcome chains and contextual integration.

links.effect: Standalone model accuracy ranged from 0.403 to 0.777 across domains.
links.quote: Model accuracy ranged from 0.403 to 0.777 across domains.

links.outcome: accuracy and intervention rate across confidence and disagreement deferral modes
links.effect: predictions with confidence >0.8 showed 16.78% to 29.23% higher accuracy than <=0.8 across six domains; disagreement trigger reduced intervention (0.083 to 0.467) with 0.650 to 0.842 accuracy
links.quote: Across the six domains (DB, SB-IRSG, PB, RB, OB, AB), model predictions with confidence scores above 0.8 consistently showed substantially higher accuracy than those with scores ≤ 0.8, with performance gaps ranging from 16.78% to 29.23% (Appendix 5).

unlisted_practices: Disagreement Trigger Mode (triggering human review when two distinct LLMs produce conflicting risk-of-bias classifications)
Reasoning Support Mode (combining LLM-extracted evidence with model reasoning explanations to assist human evaluators)

screen.practice: human-AI collaboration modes and disagreement-triggered human review
screen.reason: The study empirically tests different Human-AI collaboration workflows (evidence extraction vs. reasoning support vs. disagreement-triggered human intervention) for risk of bias assessment in clinical evidence synthesis.
